items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: It's occasionally Zoot and Al or Stan at a club somewhere. ... Stan wasn't there, Zoot wasn't there? ... Stan was there later. ... I didn't arrive at it until Stan did it with Mickey One

ctx.x: New York scene as far as Jazz goes, you make it a point to know what's happening just because you're part of that, but from what I've been able to observe in various people who I respect, it's very easy to get away from that, if you're not really immersed in it.

You can only be immersed in it if you're working in it and that didn't happen. And then for publicity and even in clubs, when you read the reviews in the New York Times, it's never that. It's occasionally Zoot and Al or Stan at a club somewhere.
Yeah, you read about established people, you don't read about up and coming people that much, except somebody who becomes the darling of the critics or something like that.
